title: A programming approach to collective autonomy
venue: Journal of Sensor and Actuator Networks
authors: Roberto Casadei, Gianluca Aguzzi, Mirko Viroli
description: This paper defines an agent control architecture for aggregate multi-agent systems and discusses how aggregate computing supports both individual and collective autonomy.

title: Towards reinforcement learning-based aggregate computing
venue: International Conference on Coordination Languages and Models
authors: Gianluca Aguzzi, Roberto Casadei, Mirko Viroli
description: This work proposes integrating reinforcement learning with aggregate computing to enable collective systems to learn and adapt their behaviors dynamically in uncertain environments.

title: Scafi: A scala DSL and toolkit for aggregate programming
venue: SoftwareX
authors: Roberto Casadei, Mirko Viroli, Gianluca Aguzzi, Danilo Pianini
description: This paper introduces ScaFi, a Scala-based domain-specific language and toolkit for engineering large-scale distributed systems using the aggregate programming paradigm.

title: A field-based computing approach to sensing-driven clustering in robot swarms
venue: Swarm Intelligence
authors: Gianluca Aguzzi, Giorgio Audrito, Roberto Casadei, Ferruccio Damiani, Gianluca Torta, Mirko Viroli
description: This paper presents a field-based approach for robot swarms to achieve robust and scalable clustering based on local sensing and aggregate programming.

title: Dynamic decentralization domains for the internet of things
venue: IEEE Internet Computing
authors: Gianluca Aguzzi, Roberto Casadei, Danilo Pianini, Mirko Viroli
description: This paper proposes dynamic decentralization domains (3D) as a mechanism to manage and adjust the scope of decentralized coordination in IoT systems.

title: MacroSwarm: A field-based compositional framework for swarm programming
venue: Logical Methods in Computer Science
authors: Gianluca Aguzzi, Roberto Casadei, Mirko Viroli
description: Introduces MacroSwarm, a Scala-based framework that enables the compositional design of complex swarm behaviors using field-based abstractions and aggregate computing.

title: Field-informed reinforcement learning of collective tasks with graph neural networks
venue: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Autonomic Computing and Self-Organizing Systems (ACSOS)
authors: Gianluca Aguzzi, Mirko Viroli, Lukas Esterle
description: Proposes a framework that leverages aggregate computing fields to provide local spatial context to Graph Neural Networks, improving reinforcement learning for collective tasks.

title: Software engineering for collective cyber-physical ecosystems
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
authors: Roberto Casadei, Gianluca Aguzzi, Giorgio Audrito, Ferruccio Damiani, Danilo Pianini, Giordano Scarso, Gianluca Torta, Mirko Viroli
description: Outlines a software engineering methodology for collective cyber-physical ecosystems, focusing on the coordination and adaptive management of large-scale distributed systems.

title: FBFL: A field-based coordination approach for data heterogeneity in federated learning
venue: Logical Methods in Computer Science
authors: Davide Domini, Gianluca Aguzzi, Lukas Esterle, Mirko Viroli
description: FBFL proposes a field-based coordination strategy for federated learning to handle data heterogeneity by leveraging spatial relationships and local model aggregation.

title: Privacy-preserving LLM-based chatbots for hypertensive patient self-management
venue: Smart Health
authors: Sara Montagna, Stefano Ferretti, Lorenz Cuno Klopfenstein, Michelangelo Ungolo, Martino Francesco Pengo, Gianluca Aguzzi, Matteo Magnini
description: This research presents a privacy-preserving framework for LLM-based chatbots designed to assist hypertensive patients in self-managing their condition securely.

title: A Reusable Simulation Pipeline for Many-Agent Reinforcement Learning
venue: 2024 28th International Symposium on Distributed Simulation and Real Time Applications (DS-RT)
authors: Davide Domini, Gianluca Aguzzi, Danilo Pianini, Mirko Viroli
description: This work introduces a modular and reusable simulation pipeline that facilitates the training and evaluation of reinforcement learning algorithms in many-agent systems.

title: Neighbor-based decentralized training strategies for multi-agent reinforcement learning
venue: Proceedings of the 40th ACM/SIGAPP Symposium on Applied Computing
authors: Nicolò Malucelli, Davide Domini, Gianluca Aguzzi, Mirko Viroli
description: This study explores decentralized training strategies for multi-agent reinforcement learning where agents learn and share knowledge only with their immediate neighbors to improve scalability.

title: A Fine-Tuning Pipeline with Small Conversational Data for Healthcare Chatbot
venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Medicine
authors: Gianluca Aguzzi, Matteo Magnini, Martino Francesco Pengo, Mirko Viroli, Sara Montagna
description: This paper proposes a fine-tuning pipeline for developing small, privacy-preserving healthcare chatbots that can be deployed locally using limited conversational data, addressing concerns about privacy and reliability in remote LLM services.

title: A language-based approach to macroprogramming for iot systems through large language models
venue: ACM Transactions on Internet of Things
authors: Gianluca Aguzzi, Nicolas Farabegoli, Mirko Viroli
description: This paper explores leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) for macroprogramming IoT systems, providing a language-based approach to simplify the coordination of multiple devices and capture global system behaviors.

title: A Field-based Approach for Runtime Replanning in Swarm Robotics Missions
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Autonomic Computing and Self-Organizing Systems (ACSOS)
authors: Gianluca Aguzzi, Martina Baiardi, Angela Cortecchia, Branko Miloradovic, Alessandro Papadopoulos, Danilo Pianini, Mirko Viroli
description: This paper introduces a field-based coordination strategy to enable runtime task replanning in swarm robotics missions using aggregate computing, ensuring adaptivity and robustness against robot failures in unpredictable environments.

title: SHAC++: A Neural Network to Rule All Differentiable Simulators
venue: FRONTIERS IN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND APPLICATIONS
authors: Francesco Bertolotti, Gianluca Aguzzi, Walter Cazzola, Mirko Viroli, others
description: This paper presents SHAC++, a neural network-based framework that improves reinforcement learning efficiency by removing the requirement for fully differentiable environments and extending support to multi-agent scenarios.

title: Exploiting GenAI for plan generation in BDI agents
venue: FRONTIERS IN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND APPLICATIONS
authors: Giovanni Ciatto, Gianluca Aguzzi, Riccardo Battistini, Martina Baiardi, Samuele Burattini, Alessandro Ricci, others
description: This paper investigates the integration of Generative AI into Belief-Desire-Intention (BDI) agents to autonomously generate plans, leveraging the natural language understanding and reasoning capabilities of LLMs to enhance agent adaptability.

title: Scaling swarm coordination with gnns—how far can we go?
venue: AI
authors: Gianluca Aguzzi, Davide Domini, Filippo Venturini, Mirko Viroli
description: This paper investigates the scalability limits of decentralized swarm robotics coordination using Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), exploring how these models perform as the number of agents increases significantly.

title: RAG-Enhanced Open SLMs for Hypertension Management Chatbots
venue: Journal of Medical Systems
authors: Gianluca Aguzzi, Matteo Magnini, Aqila Farahmand, Stefano Ferretti, Martino Francesco Pengo, Sara Montagna
description: The study presents a medical chatbot system for hypertension management that leverages Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to enhance the reliability and accuracy of open-source Small Language Models (SLMs).

title: Decentralized proximity-aware clustering for collective self-federated learning
venue: Internet of Things
authors: Davide Domini, Nicolas Farabegoli, Gianluca Aguzzi, Mirko Viroli, Lukas Esterle
description: This work proposes a decentralized, proximity-aware clustering mechanism for IoT devices to enable autonomous, self-organizing federated learning in networks with localized communication.

title: Unraveling creativity through variability: A comparison of LLMs and humans in an educational Q&A scenario
venue: Technology, Knowledge and Learning
authors: Michele Braccini, Gianluca Aguzzi, Paolo Baldini
description: This research compares the creative output of Large Language Models (LLMs) and humans in educational settings by analyzing response variability to determine how LLMs simulate human-like creativity.
